title: Area of Compound Shapes
keyIdea: A compound (rectilinear) shape is made of rectangles joined together, like an L. Area is additive: cut the shape into rectangles that do not overlap, find each area with length × width, and add them. Any cut that makes rectangles gives the same total. When a side has no length marked, work it out from the opposite sides, for example 10 cm − 4 cm = 6 cm. You can also take away: find the area of the whole big rectangle, then subtract the missing corner. Area is measured in square units such as cm².
familyTip: Draw an L-shaped room plan on squared paper, or measure a real L-shaped rug or garden bed with a tape measure. Ask your child to find its area two ways: by cutting it into two rectangles, and by imagining the full rectangle and taking the missing corner away. Check together that both answers match.

visual.caption: Is each one a good way to find the area of an L-shape? Drag each card, or tap it and then a box.

items: Cut it into two rectangles and add their areas
Fill the big rectangle, then take away the missing corner
Add up all the side lengths
Count every square on a grid

lab.caption: Flagship lab: paint an L-shape square by square, cut it into rectangles two ways, find missing sides, and take a corner away.

kid: Area is how much flat space a shape covers. We count it in squares. A square with 1 cm sides is 1 square centimetre, written 1 cm². An L-shape on a grid can be counted square by square, but that is slow.

A faster way is to cut the L into two rectangles. Cut from the inside corner, so both pieces are rectangles. Find each area with length times width. Then add the two areas. If you cut the other way, you get different pieces but the same total.
Sometimes a side has no number on it. Look at the sides opposite it. If the bottom is 10 cm and the top part is 4 cm, the step must be 10 take away 4, which is 6 cm.
You can also take away. Draw the whole big rectangle round the L and find its area. Then find the area of the missing corner and take it away. Both ways give the same answer.
adult: Ages 8 to 9. This is US Common Core 3.MD.C.7d: recognise area as additive and find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas. It builds on Year 4 and Year 5 area in the National Curriculum in England (counting squares, then the area of rectangles in cm² and m²) and comes before Year 6 compound shapes. Key words: area, square centimetre (cm²), rectilinear, compound shape, decompose, rectangle, length, width, opposite sides.

The lab has five tasks. Children paint all 36 squares of an L-shape that fits in an 8 by 6 box. They drag a cut and find that only a cut from the inside corner leaves two rectangles: 5 × 6 + 3 × 2 = 36, or 5 × 4 + 8 × 2 = 36. Then they find two unmarked sides of a 10 cm by 7 cm L-shape from the opposite sides. Last, they fill the 70 cm² big rectangle and take away the 18 cm² corner to get 52 cm².

Common mistakes. The most common is to multiply the two longest sides, as if the corner were still there. Other slips: adding the side lengths (that is perimeter), adding a missing side instead of subtracting (10 + 4 instead of 10 − 4), counting an overlap twice, adding the corner in the take-away method, and writing cm instead of cm². Be careful that every cut leaves rectangles; a cut in the wrong place leaves a piece that is still an L.

practice.prompt: An L-shape fits inside an 8 cm by 6 cm box, with a corner missing. Is its area 48 cm²?
choices: No, it is less, because a corner is missing
practice.hint: How many squares did you paint in the lab compared with the 48 in the full box?
practice.explain: 8 × 6 = 48 is the whole box. The L covers only 36 of those squares, because a 3 by 4 corner is missing.

practice.prompt: An L-shape is cut into two rectangles: {a} cm by 5 cm and 3 cm by {b} cm. What is its area in cm²?
practice.hint: Find each area with length × width: {a} × 5 and 3 × {b}. Then add them.

practice.prompt: An L-shape has a bottom edge of {w} cm. The top edge is 4 cm. How long is the inside step next to the top edge, in cm?
practice.hint: The top edge and the step together are as long as the bottom edge. Take 4 away from {w}.
practice.explain: {w} − 4 = {=w-4} cm. Adding would give {=w+4}, which is longer than the whole shape.

practice.prompt: A {w} cm by 7 cm rectangle has a corner cut out that is 3 cm by 2 cm. What area is left, in cm²?
practice.hint: Find the big rectangle, {w} × 7, then take away the corner, 3 × 2 = 6.
practice.explain: {w} × 7 = {=w*7}, and {=w*7} − 6 = {=w*7-6} cm². The corner is missing, so it is taken away, not added.

practice.prompt: Which unit is right for the area of an L-shaped rug?
practice.hint: Area counts squares. Which unit is a square?
practice.explain: Area is measured in square units, such as cm² or m². Metres measure a length, and cubic metres measure volume.

pool.prompt: Where should you cut an L-shape so that both pieces are rectangles?
choices: Along a line from the inside corner
From one outside corner to the opposite one
pool.hint: In the lab, which cut position made both pieces turn into rectangles?
pool.explain: Only a cut from the inside corner leaves two rectangles. Other cuts leave a piece that is still an L, or make triangles.

pool.prompt: Sam cuts an L-shape one way and gets 36 cm². Ali cuts it the other way. What should Ali get?
pool.hint: Did your total change when you cut the other way in the lab?
pool.explain: The shape covers the same squares however you cut it, so every correct cut gives 36 cm².

pool.prompt: A big rectangle is 60 cm² and the missing corner is 12 cm². What is the area of the L-shape?
pool.hint: The corner is not part of the shape. Add it, or take it away?
pool.explain: The corner is missing, so take it away: 60 − 12 = 48 cm².

pool.prompt: Mia adds up the lengths of all six sides of an L-shape. What has she found?
pool.hint: Is she counting squares inside, or the distance round the edge?
pool.explain: Adding the sides gives the perimeter, the distance round the edge. Area counts the squares inside.

pool.prompt: An L-shape is 9 cm wide at the bottom and 5 cm wide at the top. How long is the missing step?
pool.hint: The top and the step together make the bottom width.
pool.explain: 9 − 5 = 4 cm. 14 cm would be longer than the whole shape.

pool.prompt: Why should the rectangles you add not overlap?
choices: Squares in the overlap would be counted twice
Overlaps make the total too small
pool.hint: What happens to a square that is in both rectangles?
pool.explain: A square in both rectangles is counted twice, so the total comes out too big.

pool.prompt: An L-shape is split into a 4 by 7 rectangle and a 6 by 4 rectangle. What is its area?
pool.hint: Find both areas, then add them.
pool.explain: 4 × 7 = 28 and 6 × 4 = 24, so the area is 28 + 24 = 52 square units.

pool.prompt: An L-shape is made of a {a} by 6 rectangle and a 2 by {b} rectangle that do not overlap. What is its area in square units?
pool.hint: Work out {a} × 6 and 2 × {b}, then add the two areas.
pool.explain: {a} × 6 = {=a*6} and 2 × {b} = {=2*b}, which add up to {=a*6+2*b} square units.

pool.prompt: A 10 cm by {h} cm rectangle has a 4 cm by 2 cm corner cut out. What is the area left, in cm²?
pool.hint: Find 10 × {h} for the big rectangle, then take away 4 × 2 = 8.
